name: TLV9152IDDFR
title: TLV9151, TLV9152, TLV9154: 16 V, 4.5 MHz rail-to-rail input and output op amps
summary: Single, dual and quad general-purpose op amps for supplies from 2.7 V to 16 V (±1.35 V to ±8 V). Inputs and outputs swing to both rails; offset is ±125 µV typical with ±0.3 µV/°C drift, bias current ±10 pA, gain-bandwidth 4.5 MHz, slew rate 21 V/µs and supply current 560 µA per channel. The inputs carry EMI filters, the output drives ±75 mA short-circuit, and the S versions add a shutdown pin per channel. Rated from –40°C to 125°C.

circuits.title: Single-pole low-pass filter with gain
circuits.description: A non-inverting amplifier whose input arrives through an RC low-pass. R1 in series and C1 to ground at +IN set one pole at 1 / (2π R1 C1); RG from –IN to ground and RF from the output back to –IN set the passband gain 1 + RF / RG.
notes: V+ and V– go to the supply terminals; no supply voltage or part values are given.

circuits.title: Buffer driving 100 Ω into thermal protection
circuits.description: A TLV9151 on a single 16 V supply wired as a unity-gain follower, its output tied straight to –IN. A 3 V source on +IN puts 3 V across a 100 Ω load, so the output sources 30 mA and the part dissipates 0.39 W. At 100°C ambient and 138.7°C/W this predicts a junction of 154.1°C; the part instead cuts its output drive when hot, the load pulls the output to 0 V, and the output then toggles between 3 V and high impedance as the die cools to about 140°C and heats to about 150°C.
notes: The same example is also described with 0.81 W dissipation, 65°C ambient and a 177°C predicted junction.

circuits.title: Follower with an isolation resistor for capacitive loads
circuits.description: A unity-gain follower on split supplies whose feedback comes straight from the amplifier output, with Riso in series between that output and the capacitive load. Riso changes the loop's open-loop response and adds phase margin. A resistive load across Cload forms a divider with Riso, so the output gains an error in proportion to Riso / RL and loses a little swing.

circuits.title: Low-side current sensing, 0 A to 1 A into 0 V to 4.9 V
circuits.description: The load current returns to ground through a 100 mΩ shunt, and the TLV9151 amplifies the shunt voltage with a non-inverting gain of 49 (RF = 360 kΩ, RG = 7.5 kΩ). At 1 A the shunt drops 100 mV and the output reaches 4.9 V; the output spans 0 V to 4.9 V for 0 A to 1 A. The op amp runs from 12 V, and an LM7705 connects between its V– pin and ground.
notes: Design targets: load current 0 A to 1 A, output 4.9 V at full scale, shunt voltage 100 mV at most.
The LM7705 connects between the V– pin and ground; its other connections are not given.

circuits.title: Non-inverting amplifier with supply bypass capacitors
circuits.description: A non-inverting amplifier: the signal goes to +IN, RG runs from –IN to ground and RF from the output back to –IN. Each supply pin has a 0.1 µF low-ESR ceramic capacitor to ground beside it.
notes: A single capacitor from V+ to ground serves a single-supply circuit.

operation.text: TLV9151 is the single, TLV9152 the dual and TLV9154 the quad. TLV9151S (SOT-23-6) and TLV9152S (X2QFN-10) add shutdown pins. All are general-purpose 16 V amplifiers specified from –40°C to 125°C.
TLV9151-Q1, TLV9152-Q1 and TLV9154-Q1 are the AEC-Q100 qualified versions.
Short-circuit current is ±75 mA typical and slew rate 21 V/µs typical at VS = 16 V. Output current is also quoted as ±80 mA, and slew rate as 20 V/µs.
The block diagram shows a reference current and bias circuits feeding the input stage, control circuitry, and a class AB output stage between V+ and V–.

Two differential pairs, one P-channel and one N-channel, work in parallel so the inputs reach both rails. The P pair covers from 100 mV under V– up to about (V+) – 2 V; the N pair covers from about (V+) – 1 V to 100 mV over V+. Between (V+) – 2 V and (V+) – 1 V both pairs conduct, and offset, drift, noise, CMRR, PSRR and THD can be worse there. The width of this region shifts somewhat from part to part.
Filters on the input pins reduce the effect of radio-frequency interference. EMIRR IN+ was measured from 10 MHz to 6 GHz; values at common radio frequencies are in the EMIRR table.

The junction must stay at or under 150°C. A sensor turns the output drive off above 170°C; the output goes high-impedance and the load pulls it. If the cause of the heating stays, the amplifier keeps cycling between off and on until the fault is cleared.

The output stage drives moderate capacitive loads directly; overshoot grows with load capacitance and falls with higher closed-loop gain. For larger loads at unity gain, a small series resistor between the output and the load reduces ringing and keeps DC accuracy for a purely capacitive load. With a resistive load in parallel, that resistor costs a gain error proportional to RISO / RL. Uses named for this drive: reference buffers, MOSFET gate drive, cable-shield drive.
Inputs taken past the rails do not make the output flip to the opposite rail; it stays limited at the rail the input is driving toward.

Steering diodes run from each input and the output to the internal supply lines, which meet at an ESD absorption cell; each input path also carries a 500 Ω series resistor. These parts protect the device out of circuit during handling and assembly. If an ESD or overstress event switches on the absorption cell in a working circuit, large currents and damage can follow; current-limiting resistors and TVS diodes on the supplies let the internal diodes handle overstress events. An ESD event is short and high in voltage (for example 1 kV for 100 ns); an EOS event is longer and lower (for example 50 V for 100 ms).

After the output saturates, the output devices need time to leave saturation before the amplifier slews again at its normal rate, so delay out of overload is the recovery time plus the slew time. Overload recovery time is 400 ns typical; approximately 500 ns is also stated.

For a parameter whose mean is well away from zero (such as gain-bandwidth) the typical value is the mean; for one centred near zero (such as offset voltage) it is the mean plus one standard deviation. Offset of ±125 µV typical therefore covers about 68% of units, and ±500 µV (4 σ) all but about 1 in 15,873. An offset of 675 µV at 25°C is about 5 σ, about 1 unit in 1.7 million. From the drift histogram and the 0.3 µV/°C typical, 6 σ drift is about 1.8 µV/°C. Only min and max limits are assured; units outside them are screened out.
The WSON-8 (DSG) die sits on the exposed pad with a conductive attach. Connect the pad to V– or leave it floating; any other potential is not allowed.

SHDN is referenced to V– and is active high. Logic low is V– to V– + 0.2 V (amplifier on); logic high is V– + 1.1 V to V+ (amplifier off). The threshold sits near 800 mV above V– whatever the supply, with hysteresis. An internal pull-down holds an open pin low, so a floating pin leaves the amplifier on; SHDN must not exceed V+. The inputs are high-impedance CMOS. In the single and dual each channel has its own control; in quad parts channels switch in pairs. Disabled, a channel draws about 30 µA and its output is high-impedance, which allows gated-amplifier, multiplexer and programmable-gain uses. Enable takes 8 µs typical and disable 3 µs. Turn-off time grows with load resistance; the 3 µs figure needs the 10 kΩ load to mid-supply, and with no load it is much longer.
There is one operating mode, entered once the supply is above 2.7 V (±1.35 V); the supply limit is 16 V (±8 V). The S versions add the low-power shutdown state.

Specified for 2.7 V to 16 V (±1.35 V to ±8 V), with many limits holding from –40°C to 125°C. More than 16 V across the supplies can damage the part permanently. Each supply pin wants a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor placed near it.

Fit a low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic from each supply pin to ground right at the part; one capacitor from V+ to ground does for a single supply. Keep analog and digital grounds apart and watch where ground current flows; a ground plane helps with heat and EMI pickup. Route input traces away from supply and output traces and cross noisy traces at right angles. Place the gain resistors RF and RG tight against –IN, and make input runs short. A low-impedance driven guard ring round sensitive nodes cuts leakage. Clean the board after assembly; after an aqueous wash, bake it (85°C for 30 minutes is enough in most cases) to drive moisture out of the package.
